q: A Central Government office sends a communication in English to an office located in Region 'A'. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the English communication must be accompanied by:

options.C: A separate covering letter in Hindi

e: An English communication sent to an office in Region A must be accompanied by its Hindi translation under the Official Language Rules, 1976.

q: Two Ministries of the Central Government are corresponding with each other on a policy matter. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, communications between one Ministry or Department of the Central Government and another may be in:
e: Communications between one Ministry or Department of the Central Government and another may be in Hindi or English under the Rules.

q: A Ministry is corresponding with its own attached and subordinate offices situated in Region 'A'. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, such communications shall be in Hindi:

options.A: In every case, without any exception
options.B: Only when the subordinate office demands it
options.D: In such proportion as the Central Government may determine from time to time

e: Communications from a Ministry to its attached and subordinate offices in Region A shall be in Hindi in such proportion as the Central Government may determine from time to time.

q: A member of the public walks into a Central Government office to submit an application. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, he may submit the application or representation in:

options.D: The official language of the State only

e: Under the Official Language Rules, a member of the public may submit an application or representation to a Central Government office in Hindi or English.

q: While computing the Hindi correspondence figure of an office, a letter originally drafted in English and merely rendered into Hindi before issue is proposed to be counted as Hindi correspondence. For the Quarterly Progress Report, a letter counts as Hindi correspondence only when it is:

options.A: Signed by an officer who knows Hindi
options.B: Typed on a computer in the Kruti Dev font
options.C: Originally written and issued in Hindi
options.D: Addressed to an office located in Region 'A'

e: For the Quarterly Progress Report, a letter counts as Hindi correspondence only when it is originally written and issued in Hindi, not when merely translated from English.

q: A Central Government office has compiled its Quarterly Progress Report on the progressive use of Hindi for the quarter. The report is to be sent to:

options.A: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language, directly
options.C: Its controlling office or administrative Ministry or Department

e: An office sends its Quarterly Progress Report on the progressive use of Hindi to its controlling office or administrative Ministry or Department.

q: Before visiting a Central Government office for inspection, the Committee of Parliament on Official Language calls for detailed information about implementation of the Official Language Policy in that office. The information is obtained through:

options.A: A prescribed questionnaire filled in by the office
options.B: A secret enquiry conducted by the local police
options.C: The annual confidential reports of the staff
options.D: The audit report of the office for the previous year

e: Before inspection, the Committee of Parliament on Official Language obtains detailed information from an office through a prescribed questionnaire filled in by the office.

q: A member asks what the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is required to do with its findings. Under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the duty of the Committee is to:

options.A: Conduct the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations every year
options.B: Translate all Central Government codes and manuals into Hindi
options.C: Impose penalties on offices which do not use Hindi
options.D: Review the progress made in the use of Hindi for the official purposes of the Union and submit a report to the President, with recommendations

e: Under Section 4, the duty of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is to review progress in the use of Hindi for Union purposes and report to the President with recommendations.

q: Vacancies arise in the Committee of Parliament on Official Language and its members are to be chosen by the members of the two Houses of Parliament. Under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the members are elected in accordance with:

options.A: The system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote
options.B: A simple majority of members present and voting

e: Members of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language are elected by members of the two Houses in accordance with proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.

q: After its constitution, the Committee of Parliament on Official Language has to choose its Chairman. The Chairman of the Committee is:

options.B: Elected by the members of the Committee from amongst themselves
options.C: The Union Home Minister, ex officio
options.D: The senior-most member of the Rajya Sabha on the Committee

e: The Chairman of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is elected by the members of the Committee from amongst themselves.

q: An office corresponding with the Committee of Parliament on Official Language needs to know where its secretariat sits. The secretariat of the Committee is provided by:

options.C: The Ministry of Law and Justice

e: The secretariat of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is provided by the Department of Official Language.

q: A policy question on the progressive use of Hindi is to be placed before the highest policy-making body for the purpose, the Kendriya Hindi Samiti. The Kendriya Hindi Samiti is chaired by:
e: The Kendriya Hindi Samiti, the highest policy-making body for the progressive use of Hindi, is chaired by the Prime Minister.

q: In the Kendriya Hindi Samiti, the member who functions as its Vice-Chairman is the:
e: In the Kendriya Hindi Samiti, the Union Home Minister functions as its Vice-Chairman.

q: A matter concerning implementation of the Official Language Policy across Ministries is taken up by the Central Official Language Implementation Committee. That Committee is chaired by:

options.A: The Secretary, Department of Official Language

e: The Central Official Language Implementation Committee, which reviews implementation across Ministries, is chaired by the Secretary, Department of Official Language.

q: A Union Ministry convenes its Hindi Salahakar Samiti to take advice on the progressive use of Hindi. The Hindi Salahakar Samiti of a Union Ministry is chaired by:

options.B: The Minister in charge of the Ministry
options.C: The Secretary, Department of Official Language
options.D: The senior-most Member of Parliament associated with the Ministry

e: The Hindi Salahakar Samiti of a Union Ministry is chaired by the Minister in charge of that Ministry.

q: A town with several Central Government offices constitutes its Town Official Language Implementation Committee and a dispute arises over who should preside over it. The Committee is chaired by:

options.A: The Secretary, Department of Official Language
options.B: The District Magistrate of the district
options.C: The Hindi Officer of the biggest office in the town
options.D: The senior-most Central Government officer (head of office) in the town, nominated for the purpose

e: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the senior-most Central Government officer, head of office, in the town, nominated for the purpose.

q: A Central Government office constitutes its Official Language Implementation Committee for monitoring the use of Hindi in the office. The Committee so constituted is chaired by:

options.A: The Hindi Translator of the office
options.C: The nominee of the Town Official Language Implementation Committee
options.D: The senior-most clerk of the office

e: The Official Language Implementation Committee of a Central Government office is chaired by the head of the office.

q: Apart from translating codes, manuals and other non-statutory material of Central Government offices, the Central Translation Bureau also carries on another function, namely:

options.A: Conducting the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations
options.B: Inspecting Central Government offices for use of Hindi
options.C: Running Hindi typewriting classes for clerical staff
options.D: Conducting translation training programmes for the translators of Central Government offices

e: Besides its translation work, the Central Translation Bureau conducts translation training programmes for the translators of Central Government offices.

q: Complaints reach the Department of Official Language that offices in one part of the country are not being watched for implementation of the Official Language Policy. That watching and inspection work in the field is mainly done by:

options.A: The Central Translation Bureau, through its translators
options.B: The Central Hindi Training Institute, through its instructors
options.C: The Kendriya Hindi Samiti, through its members
options.D: The Regional Implementation Offices of the Department of Official Language, for the offices located in their respective regions

e: Field watching and inspection of offices for Official Language Policy implementation is mainly done by the Regional Implementation Offices of the Department of Official Language.

q: An office organises a Hindi Karyashala for its staff who already know Hindi but hesitate to work in it. Such Hindi workshops are organised in Central Government offices primarily to:

options.A: Teach Hindi literature to the staff
options.B: Give employees practical training to do their noting, drafting and other official work in Hindi
options.C: Prepare the staff only for the Pragya examination

e: Hindi workshops are organised primarily to give employees practical training to do their noting, drafting and other official work in Hindi.

q: The agenda papers for a Rajbhasha review meeting are being issued bilingually, and the Hindi heading for the list of business to be taken up is required. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Agenda" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Agenda, the list of business for a meeting, is Karyasuchi.

q: A bilingual office memorandum is being put up for signature, and its Hindi title is required at the head of the document. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Office Memorandum" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Office Memorandum is Karyalaya Gyapan.

q: The proceedings of an Official Language Implementation Committee meeting are being recorded in Hindi for circulation to all members. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Minutes" (of a meeting) is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Minutes of a meeting, its recorded proceedings, is Karyavritt.

q: A notification is being published in the official publication of the Government of India, and the Hindi name of that publication is required in the covering note. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Gazette" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Gazette, the official Government publication, is Rajpatra.

q: An employee applying for permission to appear in a departmental examination has to obtain a certificate from his office that it has no objection to his candidature. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "No Objection Certificate" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of No Objection Certificate is Anapatti Praman Patra.

q: On the promotion of an employee, his pay in the higher post is being determined and the Hindi rendering of that process is required in the office order. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Fixation of Pay" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Fixation of Pay, determination of pay in a post, is Vetan Niyatan.

q: An employee applies for a short spell of leave for an urgent private reason, and the leave is being entered in Hindi in his leave account. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Casual Leave" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Casual Leave, short leave for urgent private reasons, is Aakasmik Avakash.

q: A disciplinary proceeding is being initiated against an employee, and the document containing the allegations against him is being issued in Hindi. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Charge Sheet" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Charge Sheet, the document containing allegations in a disciplinary case, is Aarop Patra.

q: The accounts of a railway office are being examined by the statutory checking authority, and that examination is being referred to in Hindi in the inspection note. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Audit" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Audit, the statutory examination of accounts, is Lekha Pariksha.

q: Subscriptions are being recovered every month from an employee's pay towards the fund to which he contributes for his retirement benefits. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Provident Fund" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Provident Fund, built up from monthly subscriptions for retirement benefits, is Bhavishya Nidhi.

q: A Zonal Railway officer is being directed in an office order to report at the administrative centre from which the Zone is controlled. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Headquarters" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Headquarters, the administrative centre controlling a Zone, is Mukhyalaya.

q: An office order in Hindi records that an employee has been shifted from one station to another in the same capacity. The standard Hindi equivalent of the English administrative term "Transfer" is:
e: The standard Hindi equivalent of Transfer, shifting an employee to another station in the same capacity, is Sthanantaran.

q: Which of the following pairings of a section of the Official Languages Act, 1963 with its subject is NOT correct?

options.A: Section 3 - Documents specified therein to be issued in both Hindi and English
options.B: Section 4 - Committee of Parliament on Official Language
options.C: Section 5 - Authoritative text in Hindi of Central Acts and Ordinances
options.D: Section 8 - Constitution of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language

e: Section 8 of the Official Languages Act confers rule-making power on the Central Government; the Committee of Parliament is constituted under Section 4, so pairing Section 8 with the Committee is not correct.

q: Which of the following pairings of a chapter of Part XVII of the Constitution with its title is NOT correct?

options.A: Chapter I - Language of the Union

e: Chapter III of Part XVII deals with the language of the Supreme Court, High Courts and authoritative texts; Special Directives is Chapter IV, so the Chapter III pairing is not correct.

q: A trainee counting the Articles in Part XVII of the Constitution from Article 343 to Article 351, both inclusive, arrives at a total of:
e: From Article 343 to Article 351, both inclusive, there are nine Articles in Part XVII of the Constitution.

q: A historical note records that Sindhi was included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution in the year 1967. With that inclusion, the total number of languages included in the Schedule rose to:
e: The Eighth Schedule originally had fourteen languages; adding Sindhi in 1967 raised the total to fifteen.

q: A checklist of the languages included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution as originally enacted is being verified. One of the following languages was NOT on that original list:
e: Konkani was not in the Eighth Schedule as originally enacted; it was added later, in 1992, whereas Assamese, Sanskrit and Urdu were original entries.

q: In an Eighth Schedule checklist prepared for a Rajbhasha quiz, one of the following languages does not find a place in the Schedule. Identify it:
e: Tulu does not find a place in the Eighth Schedule, whereas Santhali, Dogri and Maithili were added to it in 2003.

q: In a region-classification test for newly posted assistants, one of the following States does not belong to Region 'A' under the Official Language Rules, 1976. Identify it:
e: Gujarat belongs to Region B under the Official Language Rules, 1976, whereas Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh are in Region A.

q: Which of the following pairs (State/Union Territory - Region under the Official Language Rules, 1976) is correctly matched?

options.D: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu - Region 'A'

e: Lakshadweep is correctly matched with Region C under the Official Language Rules, 1976.

q: A historical note on the Committee of Parliament on Official Language, first constituted in the year 1976, records the name of its first Chairman. The correct name is:
e: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language, first constituted in 1976, had Om Mehta as its first Chairman.

q: A note on the Official Languages (Amendment) Act, 1967 records that it gave statutory effect to the assurance that English would continue to be used as long as the non-Hindi speaking people required it. That assurance was originally given by:
e: The assurance that English would continue as long as non-Hindi speaking people required it was originally given by Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru, and the 1967 Amendment gave it statutory effect.

q: An employee has just passed the Prabodh examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and is to be enrolled for the next prescribed course in the sequence. That course is:
e: The prescribed sequence under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is Prabodh, Praveen and then Pragya, so after Prabodh the next course is Praveen.

q: A trainee who has completed his Hindi course asks which institution conducts the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct answer is:

options.D: The Department of Official Language directly

e: The Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations under the Hindi Teaching Scheme are conducted by the Central Hindi Training Institute.

q: A Sabha was founded in the year 1918 at Madras for the propagation of Hindi in South India. It was founded by:
e: The Sabha founded in 1918 at Madras for propagation of Hindi in South India, the Dakshin Bharat Hindi Prachar Sabha, was founded by Mahatma Gandhi.

q: A note on institutions for the propagation of Hindi records the Rashtrabhasha Prachar Samiti, established in the year 1936. The place where it was established is:
e: The Rashtrabhasha Prachar Samiti, established in 1936, was established at Wardha.

q: An employee addressing correspondence to the Hindi Sahitya Sammelan, founded in the year 1910 for the promotion of Hindi, has to record the place of its headquarters. The correct place is:
e: The Hindi Sahitya Sammelan, founded in 1910 for the promotion of Hindi, has its headquarters at Prayagraj.

q: A literary note on Hindi magazines records that the celebrated magazine 'Saraswati' was edited for a long period by:
e: The celebrated Hindi magazine Saraswati was edited for a long period by Mahavir Prasad Dwivedi.

q: A Census note prepared for a Rajbhasha file asks, as per the Census of India, 2011, for the third most widely spoken language (mother tongue) in India. The correct entry is:
e: As per Census of India 2011, after Hindi and Bengali, Marathi is the third most widely spoken mother tongue in India.

q: A note on Indian scripts records that one of the following languages is written in a script which is derived from Devanagari but does not have the headstroke (shirorekha). That language is:
e: Gujarati is written in a script derived from Devanagari but without the headstroke, or shirorekha, unlike Marathi, Nepali and Konkani.
